target_customer: Developers and companies running AI agents that need secure sandboxes, storage and networking
problem: Agents need isolated compute that starts instantly and keeps state, which traditional cloud and ephemeral sandboxes handle poorly.
business_model: Usage based infrastructure for agent sandboxes, storage and hosting

founders.name: Paul Sinai
prior_employers: Large European cloud provider (via sale of his second startup)
previous_startups: Two earlier startups, the second sold to a large European cloud provider

founders.name: Charles Drappier
previous_startups: A cloud infrastructure product with an exit

competitors.name: E2B
competitors.what: Firecracker microVM sandboxes for AI code execution

competitors.name: Daytona
competitors.what: Open source sandboxes, repositioned toward AI code execution from early 2025

competitors.name: Vercel Sandbox
competitors.what: Firecracker based sandbox SDK, shipped June 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Scale to zero microVMs that resume in under 25ms with memory state preserved needs deep virtualization expertise, which the team brought from OVHcloud and ForePaaS.

defensibility.rationale: Fast resume and persistent filesystem were real engineering advantages, but several funded rivals and big platforms competed on the same primitive.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Vercel shipped a sandbox in June 2025; Baseten, an inference company, acquired Blaxel in September 2026 to pair sandboxes with inference.

market_need_then: Agent builders in 2025 needed safe code execution environments; the company said it was processing billions of agent requests by its seed announcement per VentureBeat, which is a company claim.

identity.logo: Black wordmark file on site, design not described in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and technical: 'Compute was built for humans. Agents need something else.'

branding.brand_signature: Earlier tagline 'AWS for AI agents', later 'the perpetual sandbox platform'
branding.community_and_virality: Active company blog with comparison posts against Daytona and others; no merch or fan activity found

brand_strength.rationale: Clear positioning and an active content program, but no press on the brand itself and the name sees little recall evidence.

pivots.from: AWS for AI agents with agent hosting as the lead product
pivots.why: Positioning shifted as sandboxes became the core product; date approximate and from site copy, not a stated pivot

outcome_analysis: Blaxel joined YC in Spring 2025, raised a $7.3M seed led by First Round, and sold to Baseten on September 10, 2026 with terms undisclosed. A team with prior cloud infrastructure exits built differentiated microVM sandboxes during the agent infrastructure boom, then joined an inference company that wanted compute, storage and networking next to inference. The product keeps operating.
notes: Seed date conflicts across sources (VentureBeat says about a month after the batch, aggregators say July, November or December 2025); 2025-07 used. Seed amount and lead confirmed by VentureBeat and the company blog. Competitor entries come from 2025 to 2026 comparison pages; E2B and Daytona traction then was not stated. Total funding beyond the seed is not known. Pivot is an inference from tagline changes.
